title: Did Thomas Jefferson rewrite the Bible?
summary: Josh and Chuck explore whether Thomas Jefferson rewrote the Bible, answering "faction": he did not rewrite it, but he cut and pasted his own compilation of Jesus's teachings, known as the Jefferson Bible (The Life and Morals of Jesus of Nazareth). They discuss Jefferson's deism, his skepticism of the Gospel writers, his view of Jesus as a philosopher rather than divine, his letter to John Adams calling it the most sublime moral code, and his famous quote about diamonds and a dunghill. They cover the Jefferson Bible's contents (Gospels of Matthew and Luke, ending at the burial, no resurrection or virgin birth), Christopher Hitchens' remark, the Library of Congress printing via Cyrus Adler, and its use as a welcome gift to new members of Congress. Also discussed: Jefferson's wall of separation letter to the Danbury Baptists. The episode closes with listener mail and housekeeping banter.

segments.title: Opening banter and Harper's article
segments.summary: Hosts open the new studio episode with banter about a Harper's article on the Old Testament as an allegory for the Neolithic revolution, and a personal anecdote about an elderly woman in a parking lot.

segments.title: Did Jefferson rewrite the Bible? Deism and church-state separation
segments.summary: Chuck answers 'faction': Jefferson did not rewrite the Bible but compiled his own version. They discuss his deism, George Washington and Benjamin Franklin as deists, the clockmaker God idea, and Jefferson's wall of separation letter to the Danbury Baptists.

segments.title: Jefferson's view of the Gospels and the Jefferson Bible's contents
segments.summary: Jefferson viewed the Gospel writers as unlettered and ignorant and Jesus as a philosopher, not divine. He called his compilation the most sublime moral code. The book kept Jesus's teachings and crucifixion through burial, dropping the virgin birth and resurrection and most miracles; only nine verses were left from the New Testament. Christopher Hitchens' scissors remark is discussed.

segments.title: Jefferson's quotes and the Jefferson Bible's publication
segments.summary: Jefferson's diamonds-and-dunghill quote is read. The book was found in his library, discovered by Cyrus Adler, and printed by Congress; it is still given to new members of Congress as a welcome gift.

segments.title: Closing thoughts on Jefferson and the Bible
segments.summary: Hosts reflect that Congress giving the altered Bible is odd and mention Jefferson as the first vice president who wrote Senate rules. They suggest further reading.

segments.title: Listener questions and sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts read listener questions on Facebook and Twitter, then sign off with contact information.
